answer.exemplar: A passacaglia repeats a ground bass in the bass, while a chaconne repeats a harmonic progression, often varied in the upper voices.

stimulus.body: Log: a ground of three measures repeats over a fifteen-measure span with no interruption. fifteen measures divided by a three-measure ground gives five completions. A marginal reminder adds: divide span by ground length. Four statements are offered, and only one follows from the note.

questions.stem: The cue supplied for this item is “Count completions / Divide span by ground length. / How many times a ground completes”. Which option follows from it?

options.misconception: treats "One time" as if it followed from the evidence

confuses measures with repetitions

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: fifteen measures divided by a three-measure ground gives five completions. On that basis "Five times" is the supported choice.
